questions.question: What is the expected major product when Boron trifluoride (BF3) is treated with Ammonia (NH3)?
questions.explanation: Treating Boron trifluoride (BF3) with Ammonia (NH3) yields BF3-NH3 adduct. Rationale: BF3 acts as an electron-pair acceptor (Lewis acid) and NH3 donates its lone pair to form a coordinate covalent bond.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Hydrogen chloride (HCl) into Hydronium chloride (H3O+ + Cl-)?
questions.explanation: To convert Hydrogen chloride (HCl) into Hydronium chloride (H3O+ + Cl-), the appropriate reagent is Water (H2O). Rationale: HCl donates a proton to water's lone pair, producing hydronium and chloride ions.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Molecular chlorine (Cl2) is treated with Ultraviolet light (hν)?
questions.explanation: Treating Molecular chlorine (Cl2) with Ultraviolet light (hν) yields Two chlorine radicals (2 Cl•). Rationale: Absorption of UV light homolytically cleaves the Cl-Cl single bond, yielding two neutral radical atoms.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of tert-Butyl bromide ((CH3)3C-Br) into tert-Butyl cation ((CH3)3C+) + Bromide (Br-)?
questions.explanation: To convert tert-Butyl bromide ((CH3)3C-Br) into tert-Butyl cation ((CH3)3C+) + Bromide (Br-), the appropriate reagent is Polar solvent. Rationale: The polar C-Br bond undergoes heterolysis to form a stable tertiary carbocation and a bromide leaving group.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Ethylene (H2C=CH2) is treated with H2 gas over Palladium catalyst (Pd/C)?
questions.explanation: Treating Ethylene (H2C=CH2) with H2 gas over Palladium catalyst (Pd/C) yields Ethane (CH3-CH3). Rationale: Syn-addition of molecular hydrogen across the pi bond reduces the sp2 carbons to sp3 hybridized ethane.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Propene (CH3CH=CH2) into Isopropyl carbocation (CH3-CH(+)-CH3)?
questions.explanation: To convert Propene (CH3CH=CH2) into Isopropyl carbocation (CH3-CH(+)-CH3), the appropriate reagent is Hydronium ion (H+). Rationale: Protonation occurs at the less substituted terminal carbon to yield the more stable secondary carbocation.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Water (H2O) to yield Methane (CH4) + Lithium hydroxide (LiOH) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Methyllithium (CH3Li) reacts with Water (H2O) to yield Methane (CH4) + Lithium hydroxide (LiOH). Rationale: The strongly basic carbanionic methyl group rapidly abstracts a proton from water.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Aluminum trichloride (AlCl3) is treated with Diethyl ether ((CH3CH2)2O)?
questions.explanation: Treating Aluminum trichloride (AlCl3) with Diethyl ether ((CH3CH2)2O) yields AlCl3-diethyletherate complex. Rationale: The oxygen lone pair of diethyl ether coordinates to the vacant p-orbital of aluminum.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Hydrochloric acid (HCl) to yield Ammonium chloride (NH4+ Cl-) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Ammonia (NH3) reacts with Hydrochloric acid (HCl) to yield Ammonium chloride (NH4+ Cl-). Rationale: Ammonia acts as a Brønsted base, accepting a proton to form the tetrahedral ammonium cation.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Two methyl radicals (2 •CH3) is treated with No reagent (collision)?
questions.explanation: Treating Two methyl radicals (2 •CH3) with No reagent (collision) yields Ethane (CH3-CH3). Rationale: Coupling of two unpaired radical electrons terminates the radical chain and forms a new C-C sigma bond.
